findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: TagDevice calls tagDeviceUI, which populates localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice checks the limit. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains. The next request from the same device returns nil from the cache lookup, so Authenticate grants anonymous access for the remainder of the 29-minute cache lifetime. A rejected device can therefore bypass the limit simply by retrying. Cache only successful admissions, and add a test that repeatedly authenticates a rejected device.

findings.title: Make device admission atomic with the limit check
findings.body: CountDevices and the subsequent INSERT run in separate database sessions without any serialization. With one slot remaining, concurrent requests from distinct new devices can both observe a count below the limit and both insert successfully. Those devices then remain eligible for updates even though the configured cap has been exceeded. Serialize the count-and-admit operation across requests and Grafana instances using appropriate database locking or an equivalent atomic admission mechanism.

findings.title: Requests without a device header bypass the configured limit
findings.body: Authenticate relies entirely on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached to enforce the cap, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, even when the device limit is exhausted, an anonymous caller can omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing protected APIs without being counted or rejected. Define an enforcement path for requests without a device identifier, while allowing any necessary initial page bootstrap, rather than treating missing tracking information as successful admission.
